citation: RESOLVED AS DUPLICATE OF ROW 52. Best-match primary study: Jacob, R., Hill, H., & Corey, D. (2017). The impact of a professional development program on teachers' mathematical knowledge for teaching, instruction, and student achievement. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 10(2), 379-407. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2016.1273411 (same trial already extracted at data/fulltext/jacob_2017.pdf under row 52).
report_number: Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness 10(2):379-407 (= row 52). No separate report exists.
design: RCT; teacher/class-level random assignment within 19 low-income schools; 105 grade 4-5 teachers; elementary mathematics; Math Solutions commercial PD (week-long summer institutes + 4-6 in-service days/yr over 3 yrs, >40 contact hrs/yr) vs business-as-usual. (Same design as row 52.)
problems: DUPLICATE / MIS-CODED ROW (row 53 left INTENTIONALLY EMPTY; no effect sizes carry row_id 53). After an exhaustive identification search I conclude row 53 'Jacob et al. 2017' is NOT a distinct study but the same Jacob, Hill & Corey (2017) 'Math Solutions' math-PD RCT as row 52, entered twice in the authors' supplement (S3.1/S3.2) with inconsistent codings. EVIDENCE: (1) Both Jacob rows are coded tpd_goal=(P)CK AND tpd_trainer=Res/Dev -- the two most program-specific codes, both matching Math Solutions (mathematical knowledge for teaching; trained by Math Solutions associates = a research/developer org). (2) Robin T. Jacob (U. Michigan) has exactly ONE 2017 PD-vs-student-achievement RCT (Math Solutions, JREE 10(2):379-407); her full CV (api.isr.umich.edu Jacob_CV.pdf, retrieved 2026-06) lists no separate short coaching RCT in grades 3-6. (3) No other first-author 'Jacob'/'Jacobs' has a 2017 elementary coaching/(P)CK PD RCT -- verified via OpenAlex (author-name, full-text, and topic searches), Google Scholar, and ERIC. (4) NOT sourced from Kraft, Blazar & Hogan (2018): I downloaded their full RER PDF; its included-study list contains NO 'Jacob 2017' study (the only Jacob references in Kraft 2018 are methodological/contextual: Jacob & Lefgren 2004, Jacob & McGovern 2015, Hill/Beisiegel/Jacob 2013, Jacob & Parkinson 2015). Also absent from Lynch, Hill, Gonzalez & Pollard (2019) STEM PD meta-analysis (covers 1994-2016, predates this 2017 study). (5) The four fingerprint divergences between the rows -- grade Mixed(r52) vs 3-6(r53); SES Low(r52) vs Not-reported(r53); duration Long(r52) vs Short(r53); principle self-regulation(r52) vs coaching(r53) -- are exactly the inconsistencies expected when one trial is double-entered from two different source reviews; e.g. grades 4-5 is naturally '3-6' (r53) not 'Mixed' (r52), and the trial was in 19 low-income schools (r52 'Low SES'). CAVEAT (sign that BOTH codings are imperfect): the Math Solutions paper states coaching was 'proposed by the Math Solutions team but not taken up by the teachers' and that 'the professional development did not include a coaching component', so row 53's coaching=1 is itself a miscode of this program. DO NOT extract this PDF under row 53 (would double-count Math Solutions, already at row 52). If the authors' raw dataset is obtained (see email/data_request.md), confirm whether row 53 is a deduplication target; flag to the authors as a probable double-entry. Residual uncertainty (hence confidence=medium not high): a genuinely distinct, hard-to-find or non-indexed 'Jacob et al. 2017' coaching study (e.g., from a grey-literature source review or the authors' interviews) cannot be 100% excluded, but no trace of one was found across all major databases.
